stem: A facility compares two canopy plans. The denser plan produces more inflorescence mass per square meter but poorer cannabinoid uniformity within individual plants. What is the best interpretation?
choices: Canopy density can create a production tradeoff, so the preferred plan depends on whether area yield, within-plant uniformity, or both are priority outcomes
The denser plan is automatically superior because only total mass matters
The less-dense plan is automatically superior because density cannot affect yield per area
Planting density and canopy architecture are unrelated to production outcomes
rationale: Controlled cannabis research has shown that higher planting density can increase yield per area while reducing within-plant cannabinoid uniformity, making the decision dependent on the defined production objective rather than a single metric.
